"'''Cold Hearted'''" is a song by American singer [[Paula Abdul]], released in June 1989 as the fifth single from her debut album, ''[[Forever Your Girl]]'' (1988). It was written and co-produced by [[Elliot Wolff]] and reached number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming the album's third song to top the US chart.

"Cold Hearted" is a song by American singer Paula Abdul, released in June 1989 as the fifth single from her debut album, Forever Your Girl (1988). It was written and co-produced by Elliot Wolff and reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming the album's third song to top the US chart.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Cold Hearted" is written in the key of [[G minor]] and follows a [[tempo]] of 122 beats per minute. The song follows a [[chord progression]] of Gm{{spaced en dash}}E{{flat}}<small>maj7</small>{{spaced en dash}}Dm<small>7</small>, and Abdul's vocals span one-and-a-half [[octave]]s, from F<sub>3</sub> to B{{flat}}<sub>4</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0115260|title=Cold-Hearted|last=Wolff|first=Elliot|website=www.musicnotes.com|date=May 6, 2013 |access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref>

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Paul Lester from ''[[Melody Maker]]'' wrote, "'Cold Hearted' has been fabulously cluttered up and fleshed out by [[Chad Jackson (DJ)|Chad Jackson]], weighed down with details yet buoyed up by a deliciously light, slippery beat. Simply irresistible."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Paul|last=Lester|magazine=[[Melody Maker]]|title=Singles|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/52198955459/|date=September 22, 1990|access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref>

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: "Cold Hearted" topped the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart for one week in September 1989, giving Abdul her third US number-one single.<ref name="hot100"/> "Cold Hearted" was ranked sixth on [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1989|''Billboard'''s Year-End Hot 100 ranking of 1989]].<ref name="usye"/> It spent a total of 21 weeks within the ''Billboard'' Hot 100.<ref name="hot100"/> In Canada, "Cold Hearted" peaked at number one according to ''[[The Record (magazine)|The Record]]'' magazine and number two according to ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' magazine, while in Finland, in entered the top 20.<ref name="can1"/><ref name="can2"/><ref name="fin"/>
sections.text: "Cold Hearted" topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart for one week in September 1989, giving Abdul her third US number-one single. "Cold Hearted" was ranked sixth on Billboards Year-End Hot 100 ranking of 1989. It spent a total of 21 weeks within the Billboard Hot 100. In Canada, "Cold Hearted" peaked at number one according to The Record magazine and number two according to RPM magazine, while in Finland, in entered the top 20.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The official [[music video]] for "Cold Hearted" was directed by [[David Fincher]] and spent more than three weeks on top of [[MTV]]'s video rotation list. It uses the album version of the song, with the rap section from the extended 12" version spliced in after the 3rd chorus. The inspiration for the video came from [[Bob Fosse]]'s choreography of the "Take Off with Us" scene in the movie ''[[All That Jazz (film)|All That Jazz]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=All That Jazz (1979) [The Criterion Collection] - Dual-Format Edition|url=http://www.filmfreakcentral.net/ffc/2014/10/all-that-jazz.html|website=Film Freak Central|date=October 15, 2014 |access-date=July 23, 2015}}</ref> Abdul dances for music executives with a group of semi-nude dancers. Abdul was wearing a black [[fishnet]] dress which exposed her [[belly button]] and was sporting a hat of the German "[[Kriegsmarine]]". The dance floor included [[scaffolding]] where Abdul and her dancers hang and dance suggestively. The video was filmed in the same [[Downtown Los Angeles]] location where [[Christina Aguilera]]'s music video for "[[What a Girl Wants (Christina Aguilera song)|What a Girl Wants]]" would later be filmed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cold Hearted single {{!}} Paula-Abdul.com |url=https://www.paula-abdul.com/cold-hearted-single.html#:~:text=Noteworthy%20Appearances&text=Christina%20Aguliera's%20music%20video%20for,Hearted%22%20in%20downtown%20Los%20Angeles.&text=In%201991,%20The%20Chipettes%20recorded,The%20Chipmunks%20Rock%20the%20House. |access-date=November 12, 2024 |website=Paula Abdul Official Fan Site}}</ref> The video and its "late-'80s energy" served as a visual inspiration for the music video of [[Ariana Grande]]'s 2024 single "[[Yes, And?]]".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Havens |first=Lyndsey |date=January 12, 2024 |title=Ariana Grande's 'Yes, And?' Video Is Here: Watch It Now |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/ariana-grande-yes-and-music-video-watch-now-1235580354/ |access-date=January 12, 2024 |magazine=Billboard}}</ref>
sections.text: The official music video for "Cold Hearted" was directed by David Fincher and spent more than three weeks on top of MTV's video rotation list. It uses the album version of the song, with the rap section from the extended 12" version spliced in after the 3rd chorus. The inspiration for the video came from Bob Fosse's choreography of the "Take Off with Us" scene in the movie All That Jazz. Abdul dances for music executives with a group of semi-nude dancers. Abdul was wearing a black fishnet dress which exposed her belly button and was sporting a hat of the German "Kriegsmarine". The dance floor included scaffolding where Abdul and her dancers hang and dance suggestively. The video was filmed in the same Downtown Los Angeles location where Christina Aguilera's music video for "What a Girl Wants" would later be filmed. The video and its "late-'80s energy" served as a visual inspiration for the music video of Ariana Grande's 2024 single "Yes, And?".
